answer: At the currier's bench the oil is rubbed in by hand, and the leather will not take a shine until the rubbing is done properly. Proof of currier leather via oil rub count is the dressing: a skin the currier dresses only after 18 rubs of oil, each rub worked by the currier himself. First comes the delta, rubbed at the bench; then the basalt, rubbed when the skin was dry; the anchor is the oil itself, pressed by the currier's own hand. A cheat must rub 23 false skins and press 23 false jars of oil, and the bench still dresses no leather for him.
